items.excerpt: Runway introduced Ruby, a model that generates 16-bit HDR ProRes and EXR sequences directly, or converts existing clips and generations into them. It is model-agnostic — compatible with Gen-4.5, Seedance 2.5, MiniMax H3 and other video models — so generative shots can enter a color-managed grade/comp pipeline instead of stopping at 8-bit delivery files.
items.dupe_risk: low — brand-new launch (2026-08-21), not yet covered by any trade outlet; adjacent to but distinct from the already-selected LTX-2.5 open-weights story (that is a generator with ACES HDR output, Ruby is an HDR conversion/output layer on top of any model)

items.excerpt: The Academy opened six Scientific and Technical Award investigations for 2026, including 'solvers for markerless facial capture' and 'audio spectrum segmentation and editing software' — two categories that are now effectively ML-driven — alongside artist-friendly large-scale water sims and direct-manipulation CG character rigging. Entries close September 8, with the awards presented April 20, 2027.
items.dupe_risk: medium — same outlet as the selected AccuFACE 2 card and thematically adjacent (markerless facial capture); the story itself is a separate Academy announcement

items.excerpt: Curious Refuge walks through the current crop of free AI video generators and how far the no-cost tier has moved for shot work, with a companion blog post listing every tool tested. A practical read on which parts of an AI-film workflow no longer need a subscription.
items.dupe_risk: medium — same channel published a tools-roundup video on 2026-08-14 that was already used; different tools and a free-tier angle

items.excerpt: Two unannounced AI video models appeared under codenames in public arenas, and Theoretically Media tests both alongside a newly released free cinematic reference library. Useful early signal on what the next generation of text-to-video will do for shot planning.
items.dupe_risk: medium — this channel's 2026-08-20 video was already published; back-up item only
